title: service-boundary-adr template variables
description: Values for templates/service-boundary-adr.md.j2 and templates/service-boundary-adr.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from service-boundary-adr.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

aggregate_root.title: Aggregate root
aggregate_root.description: What is the aggregate root inside that context - the entity every write goes through? A context with two roots is two services.

bounded_context.title: Bounded context
bounded_context.description: Which bounded context does this service own - Order Management, Billing, Inventory? If two contexts fit, the boundary is in the wrong place and this ADR is premature.

consumers.title: Consumers
consumers.description: Who consumes this service today? Naming them is what makes the compatibility rule enforceable; an unknown consumer is the one a breaking change finds.

cross_context_references.title: Cross context references
cross_context_references.description: Which identifiers does this service hold that belong to another context, and how does it get them - CDC replica, API call, event payload? An unlisted foreign key is a hidden join.

cross_service_transactions.title: Cross service transactions
cross_service_transactions.description: Which sagas cross this boundary, and where is each one specified? A cross-service write with no saga named here is a distributed transaction nobody designed.

domain_events.title: Domain events
domain_events.description: Which domain events does this context emit? Name them in the past tense and version them from day one - they are the public contract.

events_consumed.title: Events consumed
events_consumed.description: Which versioned event topics does this service consume? These are the upstreams whose breaking change becomes your incident.

events_published.title: Events published
events_published.description: Which versioned event topics does this service publish? Give the full names including version suffixes.

further_split_rejection_reason.title: Further split rejection reason
further_split_rejection_reason.description: Why was splitting this further rejected? Usually a single transaction inside one aggregate; say which one.

monolith_rejection_reason.title: Monolith rejection reason
monolith_rejection_reason.description: Why was keeping this in the monolith rejected? Give the property that made it impossible, not a preference - the reason is what a future reader re-tests.

openapi_url.title: Openapi url
openapi_url.description: Where is the OpenAPI contract published - the URL a consumer resolves at build time?

owned_table_1.title: Owned table 1
owned_table_1.description: Which table does this service own outright - the first one no other service may read directly? Add a line per table; sole ownership is what makes the boundary real.

owned_table_2.title: Owned table 2
owned_table_2.description: Which is the second table this service owns outright?

system_name.description: Which service does this ADR draw a boundary around? One service per record, named as the service catalogue names it.

team_name.description: Which team owns this service? One team - a service two teams deploy is a service neither team can change safely.

value_objects.title: Value objects
value_objects.description: Which value objects live inside that aggregate? These are the types that have no identity of their own and must never be addressed from outside.
